newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Gehe mulls move on Lloyds Chemists.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gehe mulls move on Lloyds Chemists.

text.p: Europe's largest drug distributor, Gehe AG, said on Friday it was still interested in buying British pharmacy chain Lloyds Chemists but was evaluating its next move.
The German group also attacked a renewed bid from its rival suitor, UniChem Plc, questioning whether the British company had the experience to handle such a major acquisition.

Gehe's comments followed a decision by Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) to clear the way for the warring predators to take Lloyds over, providing they fulfil their promises to sell off certain parts.

"We believe that UniChem would face significant risks in acquiring Lloyds Chemists, given the relative size of the two companies and UniChem's lack of experience in integrating major acquisitions," said Dieter Kammerer, chairman of the management board of Gehe.
"This is especially true in the light of Lloyds Chemists' reduced profitability and the reduced potential for synergies as a result of the DTI's ruling."
UniChem chief executive Jeffery Harris, meanwhile, called on Gehe to launch an offer for Lloyds rather than rehearsing old arguments.

"Gehe have been making these comments consistently over the past few months. There is nothing new in what they are saying. If they want to buy Lloyds, they should get on and bid and then let the market decide," he said.
Both UniChem's original bid for the pharmacy chain and a rival offer from Gehe lapsed in March after being referred to Britain's Monopolies and Mergers Commission because of competition fears.
Gehe's lapsed offer was an all cash bid pitched at 500 pence for every Lloyds Chemists share.
UniChem, which already owns 9.9 percent of Lloyds, is offering 16 new UniChem shares and 926 pence in cash for every 10 Lloyds shares. That values the company at 657.6 million pounds ($1.04 billion).

UniChem also said it had identified cost savings and revenue benefits conservatively estimated at more than 15 million pounds in the 12 months after an acquisition and in excess of 20 million pounds a year thereafter.
As well as cost-savings, UniChem said the acquisition would enable faster development of its retail pharmacy business and be earnings-enhancing after 12 months, a claim which Gehe doubted.
Lloyds Chemists, stuck in the middle of the two warring predators, advised its shareholders to take no action.

News of UniChem's renewed offer sent Lloyds shares to a record high of 523 pence, before slipping back to close at 520-3/4, up 17 on the day. UniChem shares closed 9.12 down at 248.88. Gehe shares in Frankfurt were off two marks at 109.
If either UniChem or Gehe is successful in acquiring Lloyds it must sell off, under DTI rules, specified Lloyds' wholesale businesses within three months of the completed merger.
Lloyds Chemists owns the second largest chain of retail pharmacies in Britain with more than 900 outlets.
UniChem is one of the two largest wholesalers of pharmaceutical products in Britain and also owns a chain of some 400 retail pharmacies, known as Moss Chemists.
Gehe is keen to expand its pharmaceutical retail business in Britain which it entered with the acquisition of AAH Plc in April. ($1=.6298 Pound)
